recent.statement: The FOMC will raise interest rates by 25 basis points on July 28th
recent.evidence: No signal confirms the FOMC raised rates by 25 bps on July 28; S5-S8 only confirm the meeting was scheduled, not its outcome.

recent.statement: The Strait of Hormuz will experience a significant increase in ship transits
recent.evidence: Strait of Hormuz transits were 10 per day, 52% below the 30-day average of 21, showing a sharp decrease rather than a significant increase.

recent.statement: The Kerch Strait ship transit count will drop to 1/day due to heightened Ukrainian-Russian tensions near the conflict zone.
recent.evidence: The only Kerch Strait signal reports 2 daily ship transits, not the forecast drop to 1/day.

recent.statement: There will be at least one major disruption in the Strait of Hormuz within the next week.
recent.evidence: S4 shows Strait of Hormuz transits at 10 per day, 52% below the 30-day average of 21 as of 2026-07-23 inside the forecast window, a collapse in traffic corroborated by the existence of a documented '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis' (S7).

recent.statement: The Strait of Hormuz will see a 15% drop in daily ship transits due to heightened regional tensions linked to Iran's conflict with Ukraine
recent.evidence: Strait of Hormuz daily transits were 10, 52% below the 30-day average of 21, far exceeding the forecast's 15% drop threshold within the window.

recent.statement: A major earthquake will occur in the United States within the next week
recent.evidence: No signal reports a major earthquake occurring in the United States during 2026-07-17 to 2026-07-24; the only quake-specific web item names the 2026 Sanriku earthquake (Japan), and the generic earthquake trackers state no U.S. major event.

recent.statement: A major earthquake will occur in the United States within the next week
recent.evidence: No signal reports a major earthquake occurring in the United States during 2026-07-17 to 2026-07-24; the only quake-specific web item names a Sanriku (Japan) event, and generic earthquake trackers state no U.S. major event.

recent.statement: A major wildfire will break out in the Western United States within the next week
recent.evidence: No signal states that a major wildfire ignited in the Western United States between 2026-07-17 and 2026-07-24; S2 is only a generic Wikipedia page title for 2026 Washington wildfires with no date or event details, and S3 predates the window by six years.

recent.statement: A Category 3 hurricane will make landfall in the Gulf Coast of the United States
recent.evidence: The only Gulf Coast landfalls in the window were by Tropical Storm Bertha, which made its second U.S. landfall and degenerated into a trough — far below Category 3 hurricane strength.

recent.statement: A major storm will hit the eastern seaboard of the United States within the next week, causing significant damage and power outages.
recent.evidence: The only signal is an undated headline stating a storm front "aims at" the eastern seaboard, which shows an anticipated condition rather than a storm that actually struck and caused significant damage and power outages within the window.

recent.statement: A severe thunderstorm warning will be issued for the eastern United States within the next week.
recent.evidence: The only signal is a July 28, 2026 severe thunderstorm watch (not warning) dated after the July 23 window closed, so no admissible evidence shows a severe thunderstorm warning issued in the eastern U.S. during the forecast window.

recent.statement: A Category 2 hurricane will make landfall in the southeastern United States.
recent.evidence: The only U.S. landfall in the window was Tropical Storm Bertha in Louisiana, not a Category 2 hurricane in the southeastern United States.

self_calibration.note: Published headline probability is RAW conviction (unchanged); this is the honest companion. Calibration fixes overconfidence, not discrimination — see /calibration.
